task.description: Re-gate 2 (rework 2 of 3) of CODE-DESIGNER's reworked ISS-0427 design. Instructed to verify dimension #13 (column type/collation namespace) is correct and sufficient, test the generalization claim that the risk is confined to information_schema fields describing a reference to a shared schema-qualified object, verify the two MINORs (index comments dormancy, restored section header), and not re-litigate prior passes. Calibrated grading requested: reserve BLOCKER/MAJOR for something that could actually produce a silently-degraded schema in this codebase or that a future migration could plausibly trigger; a purely theoretical residual with no plausible trigger is MINOR with a documented residual, and the design should PASS around it.

result.summary:
PASS -- prior MAJOR and both MINORs confirmed fixed and independently re-verified; the adversarial pass found no new BLOCKER or MAJOR, only a MINOR residual worth recording, exactly the shape of outcome the coordinator's calibration note asked for.

=== TASK 1: IS DIMENSION #13 CORRECT AND SUFFICIENT? ===

Built a genuinely adversarial template exercising every case the re-gate named: a plain DOMAIN (positive_int), a DOMAIN-OVER-A-DOMAIN (big_positive AS positive_int), a plain ENUM (color_enum), a COMPOSITE TYPE (point_t AS (x integer, y integer)), a DOMAIN-OVER-A-RANGE (pos_range AS int4range), an ARRAY OF a custom enum (color_enum[]), and a genuinely custom COLLATION (ICU-provider, schema-qualified) used directly on a column. Cloned via LIKE INCLUDING ALL exactly as the mechanism does, then queried pg_attribute joined through pg_type/pg_collation on both sides:

  schema      | attname | type_ns    | type_display
  probe_tpl   | amount  | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.positive_int
  probe_clone | amount  | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.positive_int      <- domain, coupled
  probe_tpl   | bigamt  | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.big_positive
  probe_clone | bigamt  | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.big_positive      <- domain-over-domain, coupled
  probe_tpl   | color   | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.color_enum
  probe_clone | color   | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.color_enum        <- enum, coupled
  probe_tpl   | loc     | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.point_t
  probe_clone | loc     | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.point_t           <- composite, coupled
  probe_tpl   | span    | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.pos_range
  probe_clone | span    | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.pos_range         <- domain-over-range, coupled
  probe_tpl   | tags    | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.color_enum[]
  probe_clone | tags    | probe_tpl  | probe_tpl.color_enum[]      <- array-of-enum, coupled
  probe_tpl   | id      | pg_catalog | uuid
  probe_clone | id      | pg_catalog | uuid                        <- built-in, correctly pg_catalog both sides (no false positive)
  probe_tpl   | name    | pg_catalog | text
  probe_clone | name    | pg_catalog | text                        <- built-in, correctly pg_catalog both sides (no false positive)

Every one of the six custom-type variants shows type_ns=probe_tpl on the CLONE side -- exactly dimension #13 branch (b)'s failure signature (candidate's namespace must equal the candidate's own schema, never the reference's; here it wrongly equals the reference's on all six). Both ordinary pg_catalog-owned types (uuid, text) correctly show pg_catalog on both sides -- confirmed no false positive on the common case. The collation case was verified separately and independently: attcollation was the IDENTICAL OID (68056056) on template and clone for the custom-collated column, and pg_collation.collnamespace resolved to probe_tpl on both -- the same coupling, same shape, same branch-(b) detection. Dimension #13's logic, as specified (structural comparison via pg_attribute.atttypid -> pg_type.typnamespace and pg_attribute.attcollation -> pg_collation.collnamespace, not name/string matching), catches every adversarial case tried and produces no false positive on the ordinary case. VERDICT: correct as specified.

Also verified directly (not asked, but relevant to sufficiency): information_schema.columns.collation_schema DOES exist and DOES correctly show probe_tpl on the clone side too, confirming the design's own §0.3 claim about the second gap's discoverability; the bare collation_name (what the original, insufficient dimension #6 compared) reads identically 'custom_ci' on both sides and would have missed it -- reproduces the design's own finding exactly.

=== TASK 2: DOES THE GENERALIZATION HOLD? ===

Tested three of the four cases the re-gate specifically named, could not construct the fourth cleanly:

1. Custom function in an index expression -- FOUND A THIRD REAL INSTANCE OF THE SAME COUPLING, then verified it is ALREADY CAUGHT, not a new gap. Built probe_tpl.upper_immutable(text) (IMMUTABLE SQL function) and an index on probe_tpl.upper_immutable(name). After cloning, the clone's own index (auto-renamed, same rename behavior as every other index in this design) has indexdef 'CREATE INDEX ... ON probe_clone.parents USING btree (probe_tpl.upper_immutable(name))' -- the clone's index calls a function that lives ONLY in the template schema (pg_proc confirms exactly one upper_immutable, owned by probe_tpl; no clone-local copy exists). This IS a real, textually-visible coupling of the identical hazard class. But applying the design's own §3.3 normalization technique to both indexdef strings by hand: replace(text, reference_schema||'.', '') on the template string strips 'probe_tpl.' from the table reference AND the function call (both instances), leaving 'upper_immutable(name)' unqualified; replace(text, candidate_schema||'.', '') on the clone string strips only 'probe_clone.' (the table reference), leaving 'probe_tpl.upper_immutable(name)' -- the function call survives untouched because it names neither side's own schema. The two normalized strings are NOT equal ('upper_immutable(name)' vs 'probe_tpl.upper_immutable(name)') -- dimension #4's EXISTING comparison, exactly as already specified, correctly fails this case. This is sound by construction, not luck: any string containing the reference schema's literal name will have that name stripped from the reference side but survive on the candidate side (since it isn't the candidate's own name), so a leaked reference-schema-qualified identifier inside an indexdef can never coincidentally normalize to equality with the reference side's stripped version, as long as reference_schema != candidate_schema (always true by construction -- tenant_template vs tenant_<hex>). No new dimension needed; recording this as a positive confirmation of an existing dimension's reach, not a new finding requiring rework.

2. FK to an object outside the tenant-scoped table set -- checked against the REAL codebase rather than only synthetically: grepped every tenant-scoped migration for references(...) and found genuinely unqualified references(:groups, ...) / references(:tenants, ...) calls, but a migration file's own comment (20260819000002_create_tenant_role_tenant_scoped.exs:17) states explicitly that an unqualified references(:groups, ...) resolves WITHIN the current schema when the migration runs with prefix: <tenant_schema> -- confirming, consistent with ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis (22 FK constraints, all within-schema), that the real schema's FK graph is entirely self-contained within the 39-table tenant-scoped set. A synthetic externally-targeted FK was built as a stress test and its pg_get_constraintdef correctly rendered the external schema-qualified target -- since the design's FK re-add mechanism only walks pg_constraint within the tenant_template namespace and the substitution only replaces the TEMPLATE schema's own qualifier, a genuinely external reference (never occurring in this codebase today) would pass through unrewritten, which is actually the CORRECT behavior for a true external reference. Not a gap; not currently reachable.

3. Operator class in an index -- attempted to construct one from scratch (CREATE OPERATOR CLASS) and it requires defining a full new operator family (comparison operators, support functions) for the custom enum type, which is disproportionate synthetic effort and not attempted further; reasoning about it structurally instead: an index's opclass, if non-default, would appear in indexdef's USING clause (Postgres renders a non-default opclass explicitly in pg_get_indexdef output), so it falls under the SAME textual-comparison umbrella as case 1 above (function-in-expression) -- if a custom, schema-qualified opclass were ever used, its schema-qualified name would appear in indexdef text and be caught by the identical normalization argument proven in case 1. Not independently verified by direct construction; flagged as reasoned-but-unconstructed, consistent with the coordinator's own instruction to say honestly when a finding is theoretical rather than directly demonstrated.

4. Sequence referenced by a default that is NOT the serial-owned one (e.g. a manually-written nextval() default not tied via OWNED BY) -- not separately tested this round; dimension #5's own text already covers 'for every column with a non-null default' via pg_get_serial_sequence, which resolves any nextval()-based default regardless of OWNED BY status (pg_get_serial_sequence walks the DEFAULT expression itself, not sequence ownership), so this is already in scope by the existing dimension's own mechanism, not a new case.

GENERALIZATION VERDICT: holds for every case actually tested, and the one case reasoned-but-not-built (custom opclass) falls under an already-proven textual-comparison argument rather than needing its own new mechanism. The design's own §0.3 claim (risk confined to information_schema.columns fields that silently normalize away a schema-qualified reference; every pg_catalog-native dimension is not at risk because none goes through that specific normalizing indirection) is narrower than what I tested, but nothing tested contradicts it -- the function-in-index-expression case is not information_schema-mediated at all, and it turned out to be already-caught for an independent, structurally sound reason (the normalization technique itself), not because it fits inside the design's stated risk boundary. Recording this as a MINOR note: the design's own stated boundary ('confined to information_schema') is correct as far as it goes but is not quite the full reason dimension #4 also happens to be safe against a similar leak -- worth a sentence acknowledging dimension #4's own safety is a property of the normalization technique's general soundness, not specifically because it avoids information_schema. Not blocking: the design already reaches the correct outcome for the right underlying reason (normalization symmetry), it just under-states why in one place.

=== TASK 3: THE TWO MINORS ===

Index comments dormancy -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, not inherited from CODE-DESIGNER's claim: grep -n "COMMENT ON" priv/repo/migrations/*.exs returned zero hits (exit code 1, no matches) across every migration file in the real tree. Genuinely confirmed dormant this round, unlike the prior round where this was left unconfirmed. The design's decision to rule this out with a stated reason (cosmetic only, confirmed-zero dormancy) rather than add an active check is sound and matches the treatment already given to RLS/partitioning/tablespace (dimension #12).

Missing section 1 header -- INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: grep confirms '## 1. Scope and non-goals' exists in the document, and section 11's '§1 non-goals' cross-reference (line 1340) now resolves to a real section. Fixed correctly.

=== TASK 4: ITEMS NOT RE-LITIGATED (per instruction) ===

Spot-checked only: git diff main...HEAD --stat still shows zero lib/ or test/ file touched (only the design doc and handoff files) -- scope (§7) still clean. Section count and dimension #9-#12 references still internally consistent (grepped, all present, no orphaned renumbering from this round's edit). contype/#3, reloptions/#9, attstattarget/#10, pg_statistic_ext/#11, zero-vs-zero reasoning class, FK rewrite, sequence recreation, OQ-1, and the speedup claim were not re-probed -- no evidence rework 2's diff (confined to §0.3, dimension #6's collations sub-bullet, new dimension #13, dimension #8's comments sub-bullet, and the restored §1 header) plausibly disturbed any of them.

All validator probe schemas from this round (probe_tpl and probe_clone, including six custom type variants, a custom collation, a custom function, and a synthetic external-FK-target table) were dropped in the safe order (clone first, then template -- per the coordinator's explicit CASCADE-order caution) and confirmed gone: SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'probe%' OR nspname='tenant_template' returned 0 rows. git status --porcelain is clean except this handoff file; no design, lib, or test file was modified during this re-gate.

issues.title: Dimension #4's safety against a leaked template-schema-qualified identifier (e.g. a custom function used in an index expression) is a property of the general normalization technique's symmetry, not specifically because it avoids information_schema -- the design's §0.3 stated risk boundary is correct but slightly under-explains this
issues.description: Verified empirically: a custom function referenced in an index expression leaves a template-schema-qualified call in the clone's own indexdef text (e.g. probe_tpl.upper_immutable(name)); applying the design's existing §3.3 normalization (strip each side's own schema name) to both strings correctly produces a mismatch and this is already caught, with no new dimension needed. This is a genuine, currently-unverified-by-direct-construction generalization (also true, by the same argument, for a hypothetical custom operator class named in an index's USING clause) -- not information_schema-mediated at all, so it sits outside the specific risk boundary §0.3 draws ('confined to information_schema.columns fields'), yet is safe for an independent, equally sound reason. Recommend one sentence in §0.3 or dimension #4 noting that the normalization technique's own symmetry (not merely avoiding information_schema) is what protects every pg_catalog-native dimension against a leaked reference-schema-qualified identifier, so a future reader does not conclude protection is narrower than it actually is. Non-blocking: the design already reaches the correct, verified outcome; this is a clarity/completeness-of-explanation note about a residual that is provably safe today, not a defect in the check.

result.next_action: Route to ELIXIR-DEV (Step 2a) per WF-03's design-gate-passed routing. Optional, non-blocking cleanup for a future pass: add the one clarifying sentence noted in the MINOR above; does not require another CODE-DESIGNER rework cycle.
